questions.question: The bisectors of interior Angle B and exterior Angle ACD of a triangle ABC intersect at the point T. Prove that Angle BTC = 1/2 Angle BAC.
solutionSteps: In triangle ABC, ext Angle ACD = Angle A + Angle B.
In triangle TBC, ext Angle TCD = Angle BTC + Angle TBC.
Since CT and BT are bisectors, TCD = 1/2 ACD and TBC = 1/2 B.
So, 1/2 ACD = Angle BTC + 1/2 B.
Substitute ACD from first eq: 1/2 (A + B) = BTC + 1/2 B.
1/2 A + 1/2 B = BTC + 1/2 B => Angle BTC = 1/2 Angle A.

questions.question: In triangle PQR, if Angle Q > Angle R, PA is the bisector of Angle QPR and PM is perpendicular to QR. Prove that Angle APM = 1/2 (Angle Q - Angle R).
solutionSteps: In right triangle PMQ, Angle MPQ = 90 - Q.
Since PA bisects P, Angle APQ = 1/2 P.
Angle APM = Angle APQ - Angle MPQ.
Substitute P = 180 - (Q + R): APM = 90 - 1/2 Q - 1/2 R - 90 + Q.

questions.question: If the side BC of triangle ABC is produced to D, and the bisectors of Angle ABC and Angle ACD meet at E, prove that Angle BEC = 1/2 Angle BAC.
solutionSteps: External angle ACD = A + B.
External angle ECD = E + EBC.
Since CE and BE are bisectors: 1/2 ACD = E + 1/2 B.

questions.question: A transversal intersects two parallel lines. Prove that the bisectors of the interior angles so formed enclose a rectangle.
questions.finalAnswer: Proven using parallel line properties and ASA.
solutionSteps: Let parallel lines be l, m and transversal be t. Interior angles sum to 180.
Sum of half-angles = 180/2 = 90. So angles of quadrilateral formed are 90.
Alternating interior angle bisectors are parallel (since alternate angles equal).
Opposite sides are parallel and angles are 90, so it is a rectangle.

questions.question: Using the properties of triangles, prove that the sum of the four angles of a quadrilateral is 360°.
questions.finalAnswer: Proven by dividing into two triangles.
solutionSteps: Take a quadrilateral ABCD and draw diagonal AC.
This divides it into triangle ABC and triangle ADC.
Sum of angles in ABC = 180°. Sum of angles in ADC = 180°.
